correctness.rationale: Given the whole common Markov diffusivity path, the N final positions are independent normals of exactly variance 2A, reducing both maxima to one scalar common scale times two independent-normal order statistics. The telegraph occupation CLT follows from a bounded-jump Dynkin martingale with deterministic bracket; its exact variance is T/lambda-(1-exp(-2 lambda T))/(2 lambda^2). Standard two-sided normal tail expansions give asymptotically independent Gumbels. Taylor expansion of the common random scale with u_N/a_N~2 log N gives a sharp Gaussian common shift if lambda~c log^2 N and the stated alternative regimes. Exact cancellation leaves logistic Gumbel difference for all lambda->infinity. Law of total variance and bounded telegraph fourth moments give the two-term variance asymptotic with correct constants. 71 separate numerical assertion groups check finite-N instances, not substitute for asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: When a common hidden environmental volatility drives many noninteracting tracers, the right and leftmost particle fluctuations mix two intrinsically different scales. The theorem identifies the exact nontrivial (log N)^2 competition, gives the full joint Gaussian-Gumbel crossover with explicit covariance, distinguishes the environment-sensitive symmetric front and robust logistic antisymmetric front, and provides all-regime sharp variance coefficients. These are interpretable measurement signatures and a natural extension of an explicitly proposed common-diffusivity extreme-particle problem; the result is not a routine single-parameter evaluation of known scalar extrema.
